problem_statement: The matcornic/hugo-theme-learn exampleSite is a Hugo documentation theme with a persistent purple left sidebar, a search box, a Basics/Content/Shortcodes menu, multilingual shortcuts, and nested Content pages rendered in a white article column. The docs team wants a consistent "On this page" section navigator at the head of the article column across the documentation pages: a small labelled nav that lists the current page's sections as jump chips styled in the Learn cyan/teal accent, with the current section clearly highlighted, plus a docs edition picker (Stable / Beta / Nightly) in the sidebar with a live readout that names the edition the reader is on. Ship the section navigator so it (1) renders at the head of the article column on the Archetypes, Markdown syntax AND Shortcodes documentation pages alike from a single shared theme partial rather than a per-page copy, (2) lays out its jump-chip row responsively so no documentation page scrolls horizontally on a 390px phone or an 834px tablet, (3) matches the Learn cyan/teal documentation styling with a legible dark-on-teal highlighted current section instead of an off-brand dark-slate slab or a low-contrast pale-on-pale card whose title collides with the chips, and (4) keeps the edition readout in sync with the picker so a reader who clicks Beta sees the readout update to "Reading: Beta docs edition". Keep the rest of the site — the sidebar hierarchy, search box, language links, the Content and Shortcodes pages, and the Hugo build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared "On this page" section navigator at the head of the article column so it renders on the Archetypes (/en/cont/archetypes/), Markdown syntax (/en/cont/markdown/) AND Shortcodes (/en/shortcodes/) documentation pages from a single shared theme partial, not a per-page copy.

The navigator shows an "On this page" label and a row of jump chips naming the current page's sections (for example Chapter archetype / Default archetype / Front matter / Publish cue on the Archetypes page), with the first section clearly highlighted as the current section.

The jump-chip row must wrap responsively so no documentation page scrolls horizontally on a 390px phone or an 834px tablet within the overflow tolerance; on desktop the chips stay a stable single-row rail.

Style the navigator in the Learn cyan/teal documentation language with a legible dark-on-teal highlighted current section, not an off-brand dark-slate slab and not a low-contrast pale-on-pale card whose title is dragged down to collide with the chip row.

Add a docs edition picker (Stable / Beta / Nightly) in the sidebar with a readout, and wire it so that after clicking the Beta chip the readout reads "Reading: Beta docs edition" by re-reading the live selection, not a value captured once at load; the reference and the original-defect leg both keep this wiring correct.
Preserve the sidebar hierarchy, search box, language links, the neighboring Content and Shortcodes documentation pages, and the Hugo build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the Learn theme's documentation feel: slim typography, the purple left sidebar rhythm, the cyan/teal accent, the understated white article column, and code-block rhythm.

Render the section navigator from a single shared partial wired into the content template so the same rail markup and captions appear on every whitelisted documentation page; do not hand-copy the markup per page.

Use stable responsive CSS for the chip row (flexible tracks, wrap, no fixed non-wrapping width, no viewport-width font scaling) so the chips and the highlighted current section wrap cleanly across desktop, tablet, and mobile with no horizontal document overflow.

Keep the highlighted current-section chip legible with a clear foreground/background contrast (dark text on the teal accent), and keep the navigator label spaced above the chip row rather than overlapping it.
Wire the edition picker readout to re-read the live selected chip on every click so the readout always names the active edition; do not snapshot the label once at load.
Do not rename the documentation site, replace the sidebar logo, remove Search, remove the language menu, or delete the neighboring Content and Shortcodes pages.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, mobile_initial, and tablet_initial protect the original Hugo Learn home page, sidebar, and search shell.
desktop_archetypes shows the section navigator at the head of the Archetypes article column and verifies the Learn cyan/teal styling with a legible highlighted current section.
mobile_archetypes and tablet_archetypes verify the navigator chip row wraps with no horizontal document overflow on narrow viewports.
desktop_markdown and desktop_shortcodes verify the same shared navigator renders on the neighboring Markdown syntax and Shortcodes documentation pages.
edition_toggle_home clicks the Beta chip in the sidebar edition picker and verifies the readout updates to name the Beta edition.
desktop_search_focus fills the existing search input to verify the search affordance remains targetable and does not overflow after the change.

mobile_nav_open clicks the existing sidebar toggle to protect mobile navigation; this state is not used as an overflow gate because the theme intentionally widens the document when the sidebar drawer is open.

change_completion: The section navigator renders the "On this page" label and the current page's section jump chips at the head of the article column, and the same shared navigator appears on the Archetypes, Markdown syntax, and Shortcodes pages.
After clicking the Beta chip in the edition picker the readout updates to name the Beta edition rather than staying on the initially-loaded edition.
design_consistency: The navigator keeps the Learn documentation rhythm: restrained heading scale, cyan/teal accent, and a legible dark-on-teal highlighted current section.
The navigator label sits above the chip row rather than colliding with it, and the palette matches the Learn accent rather than an off-brand dark-slate slab or a pale-on-pale low-contrast card.
responsive: Mobile (390px) and tablet (834px) render the navigator chip row wrapped with no horizontal document overflow beyond tolerance.
Desktop keeps the chips as a stable single-row rail.
regression: The home page, sidebar hierarchy, search box, language links, and the neighboring Content and Shortcodes documentation pages remain intact across all legs.
The Hugo build stays runnable with no console or network errors on any captured state.

metadata.design_goal: add a shared on-this-page section navigator across the documentation pages while preserving the Learn visual system
metadata.source_repo_kind: Hugo documentation theme example site with sidebar navigation, nested Content pages, search input, multilingual routes, and responsive docs layout
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable Hugo docs example site that serves cleanly and exposes stable documentation routes plus a persistent sidebar shell, making it a natural host for a shared on-this-page section navigator and a docs edition picker.

author_notes: Slot slot_111 targets docs / design_continuity / add / cross_page / L4 on matcornic/hugo-theme-learn. A shared "On this page" section navigator (docs-spec-rail) is added at the head of the article column and rendered from a single theme partial across the Archetypes, Markdown syntax, and Shortcodes documentation pages, plus a Stable/Beta/Nightly docs edition picker in the sidebar with a live readout. The reference renders the navigator on all three doc pages, styles it in the Learn cyan/teal accent with a legible highlighted current section, wraps the chip row responsively, and keeps the edition readout live. The original-defect (baseline) leg renders the navigator only on the Archetypes page, styles it as an off-brand dark-slate slab, and lays the chips out in a fixed non-wrapping row that overflows narrow viewports, while keeping the edition readout wiring correct. The shallow-fix (bad) leg additionally freezes the edition readout on the load-time edition. Distinct from slot_281 (same repo, genuine ledger duplicate), which mounts a homepage Local showcase rail.
